title: Nine minutes is enough: An accelerated fMRI protocol for reliable connectivity mapping in healthy young adults

sections.title: 研究问题
sections.text:
《Nine minutes is enough: An accelerated fMRI protocol for reliable connectivity mapping in healthy young adults》：研究问题的原文依据。

【Introduction · S0001-p1】Resting-state functional magnetic resonance imaging (rs-fMRI) is widely used to map brain connectivity, yet the field still lacks consensus on the optimal scan duration. Shorter acquisitions improve participant comfort, reduce motion-related artefacts, and streamline research workflows, but they may fail to preserve reliable connectivity estimates. Multiband imaging offers a powerful strategy for accelerating data collection through simultaneous slice acquisition (Feinberg et al. 2010; Moeller et al. 2010; Xu et al. 2013), although the trade-off between its increased sampling speed and test–retest reliability remains insufficiently understood. Identifying the shortest multiband scan duration that still yields robust and reproducible connectivity estimates is therefore essential for establishing time-efficient, standardised rs-fMRI protocols.

【Introduction · S0001-p2】Previous work has established multiband factor 4 (MB4) as the most efficient setting for rs-fMRI (Risk et al. 2021) and shown that pairing it with factor-2 in-plane acceleration preserves SNR and functional connectivity (Cahart et al. 2023). Guided by this evidence, we selected the MB4 configuration to compare it directly with traditional single-band (SB) imaging and determine the scan duration required to obtain reliable connectivity estimates.

sections.title: 研究方法
sections.text:
《Nine minutes is enough: An accelerated fMRI protocol for reliable connectivity mapping in healthy young adults》：方法与研究设计的原文依据。

【Study design, setting and participants · S0002-S2001-p1】This prospective cohort study, approved by the local bioethics committee (KB 81/2023) and conducted in accordance with the Declaration of Helsinki, recruited 25 healthy university students (13 females, age 23.98 +/- 1.16) who had no contraindications to MRI and provided written informed consent. Participants underwent two scanning sessions, one month apart. Each session included 13-minute SB and MB4 sequences, counterbalanced within and between sessions to address possible confounding habituation effects during analysis, and participants remained blinded to which sequence was acquired first. During scanning, participants were instructed to fixate on a central crosshair, stay awake, and refrain from focused thought.

【Methods · abstract-2-1】Twenty‑five healthy young adults completed two sessions one month apart, each including counterbalanced 13‑minute SB and MB4 scans. Test-retest reliability was evaluated across multiple durations using Portrait Divergence, a multiscale graph‑theoretic metric. Supplementary analyses compared Portrait Divergence with the field-standard Intraclass Correlation Coefficient, assessed robustness across preprocessing pipelines and parcellation schemes, and examined MB4's ability to capture both cortical and subcortical connectivity.

sections.title: 主要结果
sections.text:
《Nine minutes is enough: An accelerated fMRI protocol for reliable connectivity mapping in healthy young adults》：结果的原文依据；数值与适用人群以引文为准。

【Results · abstract-3-1】MB4 consistently outperformed SB across all tested durations, with peak topological stability at 9 minutes. Stability declined beyond this point, likely due to cumulative motion artefacts. Supplementary analyses confirmed MB4's robustness across preprocessing strategies and atlas choices and demonstrated effective whole‑brain coverage.

【Conclusions · abstract-4-1】In healthy young adults, MB4 captures network topology more effectively than SB and reaches peak stability at 9 minutes before declining, challenging the assumption that longer scans are always better. These findings require validation in clinical, paediatric, and geriatric cohorts.

sections.title: 图表阅读
sections.text:
《Nine minutes is enough: An accelerated fMRI protocol for reliable connectivity mapping in healthy young adults》：图表的原始标题与说明。

【Figure 1. · F0001】Figure 1. Topological stability (portrait divergence) by method and scan duration.Split violin plot depicting the distribution of Portrait Divergence values across different trimmed scan durations (in minutes) for Multiband factor 4 (MB4) and Single-band (SB) acquisition methods. Violin shapes illustrate the kernel density estimates for each method, with jittered dots representing individual observations. Black point-ranges indicate mean values with 95% confidence intervals. Sample sizes (n) reported at the top of the plot indicate the number of subjects retained after post-censoring quality control for each duration and acquisition method. The resulting variation reflects the strict quality-control criteria applied in the main analysis. Importantly, the same pattern is reproduced under more permissive motion thresholds, yielding balanced-cohort analyses. This demonstrates that the observed findings are robust to specific data-quality constraints and the associated sample-size differences (see Supplementary Material, Section 5: Stability Analyses under Parcellation Scheme and Data-Quality Constraints).

【Data processing and statistical analysis · S0002-S2003-p4】Most statistical procedures were implemented using R (accessed via rpy2 from Python). Specifically, mixed-effects models were fit using the lme4 (Bates et al. 2015) and lmerTest (Kuznetsova et al. 2017) packages, and ANOVA was conducted using car (Fox and Weisberg 2019). Nonlinear curve fitting was performed in Python using scipy.optimise.curve_fit (Virtanen et al. 2020). Portrait Divergence was computed using the Python implementation provided by the original authors (Bagrow and Bollt 2019), available at https://github.com/bagrow/network-portrait-divergence.
